explanation: `eval()` sets `self.training = False` on every submodule, and only layers that check that flag change: dropout becomes the identity, and batch norm uses (and stops updating) its running statistics. It does nothing to autograd. Gradients are still recorded unless you also use `torch.no_grad()` or `torch.inference_mode()`, and the parameters can still be changed. Forgetting `eval()` makes validation scores noisy and batch-size dependent; forgetting `no_grad()` only wastes memory and time.
